name: Forbidden Peak
blurb: A knife-edge granite ridge above Boston Basin and one of the most sought-after alpine climbs in the range.
permit: Overnight camps in Boston Basin need a North Cascades NP wilderness permit, and summer weekends fill early. No parking pass needed on the Cascade River Road.

links.label: North Cascades NP wilderness trip planner

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.summary: A steep couloir off the Forbidden Glacier leads to an airy granite ridge, mostly class 4 with a few 5.6 steps. Most accidents happen on the descent of the same ridge and couloir.
skills: Leading and simul-climbing low fifth-class rock with big exposure
Steep snow, a bergschrund and moats with crampons
Multiple rappels, often late in the day

line.source: Placed by hand on terrain data and published route descriptions; not surveyed

waypoints.name: Boston Basin TH
waypoints.note: A turnout on the left near milepost 22 of the Cascade River Road, below Johannesburg.

waypoints.name: Boston Basin high camp
waypoints.note: Moraine and heather benches with a composting toilet nearby. Mountain goats are habituated to people here: pee on rock, not soil.

sections.note: An old mining road, then a steep, rooty climbers path with several stream crossings up into the meadows of Boston Basin.
North over moraine and up the small Forbidden Glacier.
The West Ridge couloir: 40–50° snow over a bergschrund and moat. Turns to loose rock by late summer.
The ridge crest: mostly class 4 with 5.6 steps and long drops on both sides.

pois.name: Bergschrund and moat
pois.note: Changes through the season; late in summer it can block the couloir.

pois.name: West Ridge crest
pois.note: Exposed granite with fixed rappel anchors. Slow parties stack up here.
